name: MMBench-Video
intro: MMBench-Video是一个用于严格评估大型视觉语言模型（LVLMs）视频理解能力的定量基准。该基准包含来自YouTube的长视频和自由形式的问题，更贴近实际应用场景，旨在严谨评估模型的视频理解水平。所有问题均由人工根据精心构建的能力分类法进行标注。
org: Zhejiang University, Shanghai AI Laboratory, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, CPII under InnoHK
build_method: YouTube视频采集、人工多问答标注与交叉验证、四次GPT-4V随机单帧时序必要性过滤、人工复核
metric: GPT-4语义评判0–3分；按26项叶子能力与九项二级维度报告ALL/VALID多标签均值
eval_feature: 长视频理解、时序必要性过滤、多问答Pack解析、缺失或评判失败记−1、ALL/VALID双口径
build_method_en: YouTube collection, human multi-QA authoring and cross-validation, four-seed GPT-4V random-frame temporal filtering, and manual review
eval_feature_en: Long-video understanding, temporal-indispensability filtering, packed multi-QA parsing, −1 failure sentinel, and ALL/VALID reporting
intro_en: MMBench-Video is a quantitative benchmark designed to rigorously evaluate the video understanding capabilities of large vision-language models (LVLMs). It includes long videos from YouTube and open-ended questions, reflecting real-world scenarios, and aims to provide a thorough assessment of models' video comprehension. All questions are manually annotated based on a carefully constructed taxonomy of abilities.

drawio_review_note: Primary-source audit pins arXiv:2406.14515v3 (PDF SHA-256 b3c1b7dcdb0fb870a424109c1f04f157d944e8599bd35e813981c194154add2c), the first complete Hugging Face video-package commit 78bfb7c7f93a5ab1b0d587dc5f3754eaaea2c66d and latest audited commit ef35e21df54488715a906c7e47146f5d9f4abbed (TSV SHA-256 95637acd06f70a2f6254946b7e568b646569e86cbe8968706a725c39855d4952), first VLMEvalKit integration 796dc7cd93fa06afe45f4bb7b15140c4498dc1f5, and current boundary 7055d3010c38ccb5dcae1bc9535ca19c7fe5d79f. The paper-backed construction is: volunteer YouTube collection across 16 major categories; rejection below 30 seconds; no stated upper bound for collected videos but every QA evidence clip is at most six minutes; a three-level perception/reasoning taxonomy with nine L2 and 26 leaf abilities; multiple independent human-authored free-form QA pairs per video under five rules and cross-validation; four random-seed single-frame GPT-4V trials per QA; GPT-4 0–3 grading; removal at mean ≥2.5 (246 QA pairs); and manual verification, yielding 609 videos and 1,998 QA pairs. The paper has an internal duration conflict: its main construction/statistics text says 30 seconds to six minutes, while the appendix datasheet says instances begin at 16.9 seconds. The released TSV was independently checked as 1,998 rows, 609 videos, 26 leaves, no missing required fields or duplicate indices, but it exposes 19 distinct video_type values rather than the paper's 16 major categories. The paper says CC BY-NC 4.0 while the Hugging Face card says CC BY 4.0, so the conflict is surfaced rather than normalized. The first evaluator defaults to eight interior chronological frames, supports packed JSON multi-question and direct single-question prompting, maps missing/parse/judge failures to −1, and computes multi-label leaf/L2 means. Its istype helper executes eval on untrusted judge text before checking int, an arbitrary-code-execution boundary; the evaluator then separately calls int(response), so plain integer text is stored without enforcing 0–3 while an expression can execute first and then abort conversion. Aggregation applies ALL=max(score,0) and VALID score≥0 to every stored score, including negative integers returned by the judge as well as the −1 failure sentinel. Undisclosed annotator, retrieval, deduplication, adjudication, and review-count details remain explicit gaps. EN/ZH specs have identical IDs, types, positions, and edges. Strict generation and normalization passed; formal Draw.io, architecture sidecars, fixed-light SVGs, and Desktop PNG exports were regenerated and visually verified in both languages without clipping, overlap, or rendering artifacts. Formal publication evidence [site-a11n-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 3477×1065 (English) and 3469×1065 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 3475×1063 and 3467×1063. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
